scenes.vo: He was sixteen years old when he scored the goal that made a commentator tell the whole country to remember his name.
He became Manchester United's all-time top scorer. Two hundred and fifty three goals.
And England's record goalscorer.
And yet, the boy who could do everything never quite got the credit. And as a manager, he won barely one game in four. This is the story of Wayne Rooney.
scenes.pre: Never quite [[q0|got the credit]]. As a manager: [[q1|one win in four]].

scenes.vo: Remember the name.

scenes.title: The Boy from Croxteth
scenes.vo: Chapter one. The boy from Croxteth.
Wayne Mark Rooney was born on the twenty fourth of October, 1985, in Croxteth, a working class area of Liverpool. His family were Everton fans. At nine, he joined Everton's academy.
scenes.dek: An Everton-mad family welcomes a son in [[f0|Croxteth]]
body: Wayne Mark Rooney was born on October 24, 1985, the eldest of three brothers.
His family were Everton supporters. At nine, he [[f1|joined Everton's academy]].

scenes.vo: On the nineteenth of October, 2002, five days before his seventeenth birthday, he came off the bench against Arsenal, the champions, unbeaten in thirty games, and curled in a last minute winner.
body: Aged 16, substitute Wayne Rooney [[c0|curls in a last-minute winner]].

scenes.vo: At sixteen years and three hundred and sixty days old, he was, at the time, the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history.
scenes.title: Record file: W. Rooney
rows: [[r0|Youngest Premier League scorer]] at the time

scenes.vo: Four months later, he became England's youngest ever player. At Euro 2004, he scored four goals, and the world took notice. Until a broken foot ended his tournament.
body: England's [[c0|youngest ever player]] lights up Euro 2004 with four goals.
Then a [[c1|broken foot]] against Portugal ends his tournament.

scenes.title: The Red Devil
scenes.vo: Chapter two. The red devil.
That summer, Manchester United paid more than twenty five million pounds for him. A record for a teenager.
On his debut, in the Champions League against Fenerbahçe, he scored a hat-trick.
body: Rooney scores [[c0|three goals on his United debut]] as Fenerbahçe are beaten 6–2.

scenes.vo: But at the 2006 World Cup, he was sent off against Portugal. His United teammate, Cristiano Ronaldo, was caught on camera winking at the bench.
body: England's hope is [[c0|sent off]] in the quarter-final.
Cristiano Ronaldo's [[c1|wink]] becomes the image of the tournament.

scenes.vo: Two years later, Rooney and Ronaldo won the Champions League together in Moscow. At Old Trafford, Rooney won five Premier League titles.
scenes.foot: Plus a [[h0|Champions League]], won with Ronaldo in 2008.

scenes.vo: In 2010, the season after Ronaldo left, Rooney scored thirty four goals, and was named PFA Player of the Year.
In 2011, against Manchester City, he scored an overhead kick that was later voted the best goal of the Premier League's first twenty years.
body: A spectacular [[c0|overhead kick]] wins the Manchester derby.
It is later voted the [[c1|best goal of the Premier League's first 20 years]].

scenes.vo: There was always drama. In 2010, he said publicly that he wanted to leave United. Days later, he signed a new contract.
scenes.title: Transfer file: October 2010

scenes.vo: In 2013, Sir Alex Ferguson retired, and revealed Rooney had asked to leave again. He stayed. He became captain, and lifted the FA Cup in 2016, and the Europa League in 2017.
body: He lifts the [[c1|FA Cup]] in 2016 and the Europa League in 2017.

scenes.vo: In 2017, a free kick against Stoke took him past Sir Bobby Charlton, as United's all-time top scorer.

scenes.title: Three Lions
scenes.vo: Chapter three. Three lions.
For England, he was meant to be the boy who ended the wait. Instead came heartbreak. Penalties in 2004 and 2006. Germany in 2010. A group stage exit in 2014. Iceland in 2016.
scenes.title: England file: the heartbreak

scenes.vo: In 2015, he scored his fiftieth England goal, passing Sir Bobby Charlton's record.
He finished with fifty three goals in a hundred and twenty games. But no trophies. The golden generation never won a thing.

scenes.title: The Road Back
scenes.vo: Chapter four. The road back.
In 2017, he went home to Everton. Against West Ham, he scored a hat-trick, including a goal from inside his own half.
Then came America. At DC United, he took a team that was bottom of the table into the play-offs.
In one game, deep into stoppage time, he chased back to win the ball, then crossed for the winner.
body: In the final seconds, Rooney [[c0|chases back to win the ball]]...

scenes.title: The Dugout
scenes.vo: Chapter five. The dugout.
In 2020, he returned to England with Derby County. First as a player, then as manager.
The club fell into administration, and was docked twenty one points. Rooney turned down an approach from Everton to stay. Derby were relegated anyway.

photo.cap: Street art in Derby during the club's crisis, 2022.

body: Rooney [[c1|turns down Everton]] to stay, but cannot stop relegation.

cues.c1: turned down an approach from Everton

scenes.vo: After a spell back in Washington, as DC United manager, Birmingham City hired him in 2023.
It lasted eighty three days. Then came Plymouth Argyle. Twenty five games, and he was gone again.
scenes.title: Managerial file
The Verdict
scenes.vo: Chapter six. The verdict.
Today, he works in the studio, for the BBC. He has spoken openly about the toll the pressure took on his mental health. In June 2026, asked if he would manage again, he said, probably not.
Two hundred and fifty three goals for United. Fifty three for England. Five league titles.
He played up front, in midfield, on the wing. Wherever he was asked. Maybe that's why he never got the credit of a Ronaldo or a Messi. But at sixteen, we were told to remember his name. We did.
scenes.pre: Striker. Midfielder. Winger. [[q0|Wherever he was asked]].

scenes.vo: So, is Wayne Rooney the most underrated legend of the Premier League era? Tell me in the comments. And subscribe, for the next story.
